13-369.r: MP Online → not an e-procurement portal; it is the Madhya Pradesh Government's online citizen-services (e-Governance) portal. MP Tenders, GeM, MP LUN are the e-procurement options.

13-370.r: Cloud computing services → IaaS, PaaS and SaaS; allotment of electromagnetic spectrum is not a cloud service.

13-371.r: SaaS → buyers can customise user interface and data fields; data accessible on mobile devices; Outlook, Hotmail, Yahoo! Mail are SaaS → all three correct.

13-372.r: PaaS = Platform as a Service → cloud platform to develop, deploy, run and manage apps without maintaining the OS, tools or hardware.

13-373.r: Sky Drive → Microsoft's personal cloud storage service; now renamed One Drive.

13-374.r: Virtual assistants → Alexa (Amazon), Cortana (Microsoft), Siri (Apple); 'Cortesa' is not one.

13-375.r: Project Loon (Google X) → wireless communication: high-altitude balloons in the stratosphere (about 18 km) give internet to rural and remote areas.

13-376.r: DACNET (dacnet.nic.in) → e-Agriculture portal of the Department of Agriculture, Cooperation and Farmers Welfare, run by the National Informatics Centre.

13-377.r: IBM = International Business Machine → an American multinational IT corporation.

13-378.r: HTTP (http) = Hypertext Transfer Protocol → the foundation of data communication for the World Wide Web.

13-379.r: Protocol used for accessing the World Wide Web → HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol).

13-381.r: XML = eXtensible Markup Language → stores and transmits data in a format both human-readable and machine-readable.

13-382.r: URL = Uniform Resource Locator → the definite, unique address of every web page.
13-382.t: It is Uniform, not Universal or Unique, Resource Locator.

13-383.r: FTP = File Transfer Protocol → protocol for exchanging files over the Internet.

13-384.r: SMPS = Switched Mode Power Supply → takes rectified AC input and converts it to the low-voltage DC a computer needs.

13-385.r: UPS = Uninterrupted Power Supply → keeps the computer running for a short time after main power fails so it can be shut down properly.

13-386.r: OR gate → output HIGH (1) when any one or more inputs is HIGH; output LOW only when all inputs are 0.
13-386.h: OR: any one HIGH input is enough.

13-387.r: Given logic circuit → output C = 1: A with input 1 gives 1, B with input 1 gives 1, and these two 1s give C = 1.

13-388.r: NAND gate → Boolean expression (A.B)'; NAND = AND + NOT (NOT AND); a universal gate that can build any logic gate.

13-389.r: Minimum NAND gates needed to implement an Ex-OR function → 4.

13-392.r: Aakash → claimed world's cheapest tablet PC, for education; launched 5 October 2011; made by Datawind to IIT Jodhpur specifications; Rs. 1100 after 50% subsidy.

13-393.r: Enhancing use of IT for development → strategy of the Andhra Pradesh Government, under Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu (1999-2004).

13-394.r: Information Technology (as the book defines it) → Connectivity + Hardware: network-connecting hardware for data acquisition, information, security and design.

13-395.r: Social media optimization (SMO) → using social networks to create publicity and raise awareness of a product, service, brand or event.

13-396.r: Collaborative Filtering → predicts a user's interests from collective preferences; used in recommender systems of Amazon, YouTube, Netflix.

13-397.r: Wearable devices → identify location (GPS), monitor sleep and heart rate, and assist the hearing impaired (hearing aids) → all three.

13-398.r: Smart home scenario (alarm starts geyser, fridge orders groceries, car warns of traffic) → Internet of Things (IoT): everyday objects with sensors, software and network connectivity.

13-399.r: 5G (Fifth Generation) → enables Internet of Things, Edge Computing and Network Slicing; faster speed, lower latency, many devices at once.

13-400.r: Metaverse → interoperable network of 3D virtual worlds used simultaneously by millions, with property rights over virtual items (definition by Matthew Ball).

13-401.r: Vidya Vahini Project → takes computer education to government primary schools across the country.

14-001.r: Father of the Indian Space Programme → Dr. Vikram Ambalal Sarabhai, physicist and astronomer who started space research in India.

14-003.r: India's first satellite → Aryabhatta (360 kg), launched by the Soviet Union on 19 April 1975 from Kapustin Yar on a Cosmos 3M rocket; India entered the space age.

14-006.r: Prof. U.R. Rao → designed Aryabhatta (1975); set up satellite technology in India from 1972; ISRO Chairman 1984-1994.

14-007.r: First animal in Earth orbit → Laika, a Soviet stray dog from Moscow, aboard Sputnik 2, launched 3 November 1957.

14-008.r: 3 November 1957 → dog Laika (Sputnik-2); 28 May 1959 → monkeys Able and Baker; 19 August 1960 → dog Belka (Sputnik-5).
14-008.t: Don't confuse Laika (first, 1957) with Belka (1960) or Baker (a monkey, 1959).

14-009.r: First human in space → Yuri Gagarin, 12 April 1961, Vostok-1; Alan Shepard became first American in space less than a month later.

14-010.r: First woman in space → Valentina Tereshkova (Russian), Vostok-6, 16 June 1963; spent almost three days and orbited Earth 48 times.

14-011.r: First man on the Moon → Neil Armstrong (Apollo-11, lunar module 'Eagle', 20 July 1969); Buzz Aldrin joined him about 19 minutes later.

14-012.r: Oleg Kononenko (Russia) → record for most cumulative time in space, 1110.6 days on ISS; broke Gennady Padalka's 878.5 days on 4 February 2024.

14-013.r: NASA's longest single spaceflight → Frank Rubio, 370.9 days (returned 27 September 2023); before him Mark Vande Hei, 355.2 days (2022). The book gives no single answer (*).

14-014.r: Sunita Williams and Butch Wilmore → returned in SpaceX Crew Dragon 'Freedom' (Crew-9), splashing down off Florida on 18 March 2025 after a 286-day mission.

14-015.r: Tim Peake → British astronaut of the European Space Agency (ESA), former ISS crew member and test pilot.

14-016.r: Wrong pair: Atlantis – Space station; Atlantis was a NASA space shuttle, like Columbia, Challenger and Discovery. COBE → Cosmic Background Explorer satellite (1989–1993).

14-017.r: Curiosity Rover → Mars probe of USA; Messenger → Mercury probe of NASA; Rustam-1 → DRDO unmanned aerial vehicle; Akash-2 → Tablet.

14-018.r: NASA's last Space Shuttle → Atlantis (launched 8 July, landed 21 July 2011); Columbia broke up during re-entry on 1 February 2003.

14-019.r: DAVINCI+ and VERITAS → NASA Discovery Programme missions to Venus, its first since the 1990s; VERITAS launch tentatively 2031.
14-019.h: V for VERITAS, V for Venus.

14-020.r: Cassini-Huygens → Saturn and its rings; Juno → Jupiter; Artemis → human spaceflight, Moon to Mars; VERITAS → Venus.
